## Purpose

Pull requests reach this crate through a port: a trait plus normalised plain data, with one adapter per provider and a factory that picks the adapter from the provider in force. No command ever names `gh` or a REST host — that is what makes a second provider a new adapter instead of a new branch in every caller. The port also owns the vocabulary: refs are always short, provider state words are reduced to one `PrStatus`, and the one fact only Azure gives travels verbatim in its own labelled field instead of being flattened into the shared ones. Every operation answers `Result<T, String>` with a stable token, so an unmeasured state is never dressed up as a measured one.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/shared/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 3

Beyond the census facts, what the three exemplars show:

- **Names and homes.** The read/status half lives in `branch_state.rs` (`PrStatus`, `PrEvidence`, `PrLookup`, `ProviderPrCli`, `LocalOnlyPr`); the action half lives in `pr_provider.rs` (`PrProvider`, `PrView`, `PrToOpen`, `PrOpened`, `GithubPrCli`, `UnsupportedPr`); one adapter per provider gets its own module (`pr_azure.rs`).
- **Visibility.** Everything is `pub(crate)` — the port is internal surface. Data structs carry `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]` and `pub(crate)` fields; no serde.
- **Plain data only.** `PrView` and `PrToOpen` hold no path and no process handle: "the same shape `branch_state`'s read view has". Branch names in and out are SHORT; the adapter that needs `refs/heads/` builds it.
- **Normalisation lives in the port, as pure functions.** `short_ref`, `status_from_azure`, `status_from_github` — applied on both sides so the answer cannot depend on which adapter produced it, and unit-tested directly without a network.
- **Stable refusal tokens.** `PR_UNSUPPORTED`, `PR_CLI_ABSENT`, `PR_CLI_FAILED`, `PR_UNREADABLE`, `PR_NOT_QUERIED` are `const &str` in `branch_state.rs`; adapters return them (plus `"parse-error"`, `"gh-not-found"`) as the `Err` payload. A word outside a provider's documented contract maps to `PrStatus::Unknown(PR_UNREADABLE)`, never to a guessed state.
- **The unimplemented case is a type.** `UnsupportedPr` answers `PR_UNSUPPORTED` for every operation while still naming the provider that was asked for; it is kept separate from an adapter that simply is not written yet.
- **Factory, not a name.** `pub(crate) fn provider_for(root: &Path) -> Box<dyn PrProvider>` routes on `mustard_core::resolve_provider(root, &cfg.git.provider)` — the one spelling of that precedence.
- **Direction of dependency.** `shared` is the leaf both `hooks` and `commands` may use; the port never imports from `commands`, even when the same runner shape exists there (`pr_provider` re-writes `gh_out` rather than importing `pr_door`'s).
- **Tests.** Pure mappings asserted directly; adapters driven through a table-driven fake (`FakeTransport` recording every request, `branch_state`'s `FakePr`), asserting the request body and the derived URL. No test touches the network.

## How to apply

To add an operation: put it on the trait with a `///` line, implement it in every adapter, and make the unsupported implementation answer the stable token. To add a provider: create `shared/pr_<provider>.rs` with the adapter struct bound to one repository root, keep every URL derived from the `origin` remote rather than read back from a response, register the token in `provider_for`, and add a fake-transport test asserting the request the adapter sends. Errors degrade to `Err(String)` — `clippy::unwrap_used` is `deny` crate-wide and these run on paths that must keep answering JSON.

Must not: name a provider or a CLI outside an adapter; return a fabricated value (`number: 0`, `PrStatus::Closed`) for an answer that could not be read; map a richer provider vocabulary onto a poorer one; import `crate::commands::…` from `shared`.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/rt/src/shared/pr_provider.rs — the trait, the normalised data, the GitHub adapter, `UnsupportedPr`, and the `provider_for` factory, with the mapping tests at the bottom.
- Ref: apps/rt/src/shared/pr_azure.rs — the REST adapter: `AzureRemote` parsing every remote spelling, the `AzureTransport` seam, credentials resolved from the git vault, and no merge operation by design.
- Ref: apps/rt/src/shared/branch_state.rs — the status half: `PrStatus`, the `PR_*` tokens, `PrLookup` and the `ProviderPrCli` / `LocalOnlyPr` implementations the classifier is injected with.
